$comment: A 55-page evaluation storyline whose plan cleared every plan gate while the storyline critique rated it 5/10 with three blockers and a revise verdict. It stops at the plan - no deck was built - so it is scored on its plan alone. It is the plan gates' known blind spot kept in view: consistency of numbers across pages and a governing answer the pages do not prove are invisible to them.
name: emirates-v8

foundByLooking.defect: The answer's conditions are stated four different ways across the answer, the summary, the scorecard and the takeaway.
foundByLooking.why: The plan gates read page shapes and exhibit families; none compares the conditions the answer names with the ones later pages test.
foundByLooking.fix: One list of conditions, used verbatim wherever the deck states or tests them; a storyline-critique check.

foundByLooking.defect: Two different load factors are both called 'load factor', so the same measure reads 64.9% on two pages and 78.4% on two others.
foundByLooking.why: No gate reads a named measure across pages.
foundByLooking.fix: Label and date each figure by its basis; a claims-level consistency check across pages.

foundByLooking.defect: A rival's fleet and order book differ on every page that states them.
foundByLooking.why: Same blind spot: numbers are checked against records one page at a time.
foundByLooking.fix: One reconciled figure per quantity, with its date and boundary.

foundByLooking.defect: About a dozen titles are counts or rankings with no implication, so the title spine stalls from section 02 onwards.
foundByLooking.why: PLAN_TITLE_LENGTH measures how long a title is, not whether it states a finding.
foundByLooking.fix: A title that states what the count means for the answer.
